key_insight: A CAD mechanism that looks plausible may still fail to work. This paper studies AI-generated mechanisms through their physical function, rather than appearance alone.
problem_solved: How can AI agents turn underspecified requests into working CAD mechanisms—and verify success when different designs use different components, controls, and operating conditions?
method: Study functional CAD design, where agents interpret underspecified requests and construct mechanisms.
Iteratively revise candidate mechanisms to satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation.
Address the difficulty of verifying function across structurally different designs; the provided abstract is incomplete and does not specify the verification method.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights the need to evaluate generated engineering designs by simulated behavior, not just visual plausibility. It frames functional verification as a key challenge for reliable design agents.
visual_elements: Side-by-side CAD assemblies labeled 'Looks right' and 'Works in simulation'.
Workflow diagram: request → CAD mechanism → physical simulation → revision.
Two different mechanisms performing the same task, illustrating design-independent evaluation.
Simulation view with motion arrows and functional pass/fail indicators.
paper_title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
paper_authors: Wenqian Zhang, Yangyi Huang, Zigeng Xu, Weiyang Liu, Zhen Liu
